neighbours.label: Capacity-building language: ' capacity' (and verbs like equip) as an organisation's or community's ability that is built or strengthened, not a physical size
fire: The grant will help build national capacity for climate adaptation.
NGOs are working to build capacity among rural farmers' groups.
The project focuses on building capacity in local health systems.
We invest in building the capacity of community leaders.
Donors pledged funds to build institutional capacity in the ministry.
The workshop aims to build capacity for early warning systems.
Partners will build the capacity of teachers to support refugee children.
Our goal is building research capacity at regional universities.
quiet: The new arena has a capacity of twenty thousand seats.
The tank's capacity is about fifty liters of water.
The hall was filled to capacity for the concert.
This phone's battery capacity is larger than last year's model.
The bus can carry forty passengers at full capacity.
The hard drive has a storage capacity of two terabytes.
The dam's capacity was increased after the flood.
The elevator's weight capacity is posted inside the door.

predictions: ' capacity' after build/building/strengthen in development text reaches 0.3-0.8; physical capacity (seats, battery, storage) stays under 0.05.
notes: Probe: 'build local capacity' 0.790 vs 'build local support' 0.221; 'strengthen the capacity of health workers' 0.271; 'equip young leaders' 0.425 vs 'inspire' 0.067; 'seating capacity' 0.014; battery capacity 0.014. Card: capacity x10, all build capacity.
